paras: The lynching of two prisoners at Sylvaren, Mississippi, was the shooting of two Black men in a Smith County jail by a mob in mid-August 1888. The two were among four Black prisoners under arrest, accused of killing a white man named Lee, and were shot dead inside the jail. A brief New Orleans dispatch carried the story to papers from New York and Maine to Dakota, and a Leavenworth, Kansas, paper used it in a campaign appeal against the Democratic party.

According to a New Orleans dispatch printed by the Evening Journal of Wilmington, Delaware, a party of men had gone a few nights earlier to a house near Sylvarena to arrest a Black man "for some crime" and were fired on by "the negroes" there. Lee, a white man, was fatally shot and died a few hours later, after which four Black men were put in jail at Raleigh. The same dispatch remarked that there had been "a great deal of killing in Smith county of late." Other reports said only that the four were under arrest for Lee's killing and did not describe how he died.

The most widely printed account, a New Orleans special dated August 20, said a mob broke into the jail at Sylvaren on Friday night, August 17, to get possession of the four prisoners. Unable to get into the iron cage where the men were confined, the attackers thrust the muzzles of their guns through the bars and shot two of the prisoners dead.

The Evening Journal gave a different sequence, placing the attack on Saturday night. In its account an armed crowd told the sheriff they wanted to put a horse thief in jail, overpowered him when he opened the jail, and shot and killed two of the prisoners. Neither version named the dead men, any member of the mob, or what became of the other two prisoners.
No report of an inquest, an arrest, or a prosecution of anyone in the mob appears in the coverage.

The New York Evening World ran the wire item on August 20 under the headline "Two Negroes Shot in Jail," while the Evening Journal headed its fuller version "Lynched in Mississippi." Over the next three days the same text appeared without comment in news-summary columns of the Daily Kennebec Journal and the Portland Daily Press in Maine and the Independent Statesman of Concord, New Hampshire, and as "Two Negroes Shot to Death" in the Maysville, Kentucky, Evening Bulletin. The place name shifted from paper to paper, printed as "Sylvaren," "Sylvaron," "Sylva-ren," "Sylvarena" and "Sylvarenas."

The Mitchell Capital in Dakota gave the item a sharper headline, "MORE NEGROES KILLED," and called the attackers "an Armed Mob of Lynchers," though its subhead placed the jail in Louisiana while its text said Mississippi. The Charlotte Messenger in North Carolina reprinted the item on September 1 under "Negroes Mobbed," again without comment.

The most pointed use came from The Advocate of Leavenworth, Kansas, which on September 8 printed the account on its editorial page beneath its Harrison and Morton ticket and asked readers, "Now will you swallow that, and vote for Cleveland and Democracy this fall?" On the same page the paper endorsed the Richmond Planet's protest against the killing of "unarmed American Citizens of African decent" and declared that "The lynch-law must and will go."

The two New Orleans dispatches of August 20 disagreed on the day, the jail and the method of attack: the wire item said Friday night at Sylvaren, with shots fired through the cage bars, while the Evening Journal said Saturday night at Raleigh, after the sheriff was tricked and overpowered. The wire version was far more widely reprinted, but the Evening Journal's account is the only one that describes Lee's death and the sheriff's part, and neither came from a Mississippi paper.

reader.title: Lynching of two prisoners at Sylvaren, Mississippi
bases: A mob shot two Black prisoners to death inside a jail where they were held on an accusation of killing a white man (A1, A3, A4).

Two prisoners were shot dead by a 'mob' or 'armed crowd of men' with no lawful authority (A1, A3), and the victims were held for the killing of a white man named Lee, so the killing was framed as punishment for that crime (A1, A4).

Two distinct New Orleans dispatches, the widely reprinted wire item (A1, A4, A5) and the Evening Journal's separate account (A3), agree that a mob killed two of four Black prisoners held in a Smith County jail for Lee's killing, though they differ on details.

accounts.label: Evening Journal (New Orleans dispatch)
accounts.gist: Lee was shot when Black men fired on an arrest party near Sylvarena; four were jailed at Raleigh; on Saturday night an armed crowd tricked the sheriff into opening the jail, overpowered him, and killed two.

framing.detail: Northern dailies ran the item as a short news paragraph under headlines such as 'Two Negroes Shot in Jail' and 'Two Negroes Shot to Death', with no comment.
The Evening Journal headed its fuller version 'Lynched in Mississippi' and noted 'a great deal of killing in Smith county of late.'
The Mitchell Capital headlined 'MORE NEGROES KILLED' and called the attackers 'an Armed Mob of Lynchers', placing the jail in Louisiana in its subhead.
The Charlotte Messenger ran the wire text under 'Negroes Mobbed' without comment.

The Leavenworth Advocate reprinted the account on its editorial page and asked readers whether they would 'swallow that, and vote for Cleveland and Democracy', beside a call that 'The lynch-law must and will go.'
